metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

Agents using the `edit_files` tool (or any similar exact-string-match replacement tool) can silently truncate adjacent content when the `search` string is a substring of a longer single line. The replacement is performed correctly per the tool's contract -- the issue is on the agent side: the agent picked too short a `search` value, and the line in the file is longer than the search anchor, so the "rest of the line" past the search anchor is deleted along with the search content.

Codify the hazard as a `meta/lessons.md` entry so future agents avoid the same pattern.

## Concrete recurrence (PR #1034)

During the 2026-05-11 bug-cohort refinement session, an agent ran an `edit_files` call to add a new `### Refinement` bullet at the top of CHANGELOG.md's `[Unreleased]` section. The `search` string captured the existing first bullet body up to one line:

```
### Refinement
- **chore(vbrief): #441 close-out -- scope vBRIEF moved active/ -> completed/ after PR #441 merged at 57bab6f.**
```

But the actual first bullet in the file was longer than that -- it continued past the matched substring with additional prose (the lifecycle bookkeeping context: which skill, which file path, what status flipped, that no code changed). The `replace` block reinserted the matched search content verbatim AND prepended the new bullet -- but the OVERFLOW past the search anchor (the continuation prose on subsequent lines, technically still part of the same logical bullet entry per CHANGELOG.md conventions) was discarded because the `search` regex stopped at the period plus closing `**`.

Greptile's review on the resulting PR caught the truncation as a P1-class diff finding ("CHANGELOG.md:26 #441 close-out bullet body had been stripped"). The agent restored the body verbatim in a follow-up commit.

This is the second instance in 30 days where short-search-string replacement silently dropped adjacent content (the first was in the #911 cascade where CHANGELOG conflict resolution dropped branch entries via a `text[head_open:sep+1]` slice -- different mechanism, same outcome class).

## Recommended rule

Append a new section to `meta/lessons.md` (no separate gateable rule -- this is agent behavioural guidance, not a deterministic check):

```
## edit_files search strings MUST capture full units, not substrings (2026-05)

When using `edit_files` (or any exact-string-match replacement) to modify a single-line or
multi-line entry (CHANGELOG bullets, list items, section headings), the `search` value MUST
match the FULL line / FULL entry being targeted, including any trailing prose / continuation
that the agent intends to preserve.

Anti-pattern: pick the first N words of a long bullet as the search anchor; the replacement
silently truncates the bullet at the end of the matched substring.

Mitigation:
- ! When targeting a markdown bullet, the `search` value MUST extend to the next blank line
  or the next top-level list marker, whichever comes first. Re-read the file and capture
  ALL bytes that belong to the targeted entry.
- ! When adding a new bullet ABOVE an existing one, an even safer pattern is to anchor the
  `search` value on the section heading (e.g. `### Refinement`) and re-emit the heading in
  the `replace` value followed by the new bullet and a placeholder for the existing first
  bullet -- but you MUST still capture every byte of that existing first bullet.
- ! After every `edit_files` call that touches CHANGELOG.md, ROADMAP.md, or any other
  append-only narrative file, re-read the surrounding 20 lines of the edited region and
  verify nothing was truncated. This is part of the standard pre-commit file review.

Recurrence record:
- PR #1034 (2026-05-11) -- CHANGELOG.md `### Refinement` first bullet truncated when adding
  a new bullet above it; Greptile caught it as a P1 in review-cycle.
- PR #911 cascade (2026-05-04) -- different mechanism (HEAD-only slice resolution), same
  outcome class: CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` branch entries dropped on conflict resolution.
```

Per the Rule Authority [AXIOM] (`main.md`), this is a lesson-tier entry -- the rule body
above is the full content because no stronger encoding exists (there is no deterministic
gate that can prevent an agent from passing too-short a `search` value to `edit_files`).

## Optional follow-up (DOES NOT block this issue)

A possible deterministic-tier strengthening: add a `task verify:changelog-bullets` lint that
walks CHANGELOG.md / ROADMAP.md and asserts every `### <Section>` block contains at least
N bullets and that no bullet body is suspiciously short (e.g. ends with `.**` with no
continuation prose for a section that historically averages multi-paragraph bullets). The
heuristic is shape-only -- it cannot catch a "valid-but-shorter-than-intended" truncation
deterministically -- so the prose lesson remains the primary mitigation.

## Cross-references

- PR #1034 (the surfacing event; Greptile P1 on the truncated #441 close-out bullet)
- PR #911 (sibling recurrence; different mechanism, same outcome class)
- `skills/deft-directive-build/SKILL.md` and `skills/deft-directive-refinement/SKILL.md`
  pre-commit file review steps (the mandatory re-read that would have caught this; the
  lesson is "agent skipped that step on a small-looking edit")
- `meta/lessons.md` (the file that needs the new section)
